name: Nox-Aeterna
specific_features: Permanent dark side facing away from star
description: Nox-Aeterna is tidally locked to its dim red dwarf star, presenting one face to perpetual twilight and the other to endless night. The dark side is a frozen wasteland where nitrogen itself lies as ice across vast plains, the temperatures so extreme that conventional materials become brittle as glass. The twilight zone between light and dark offers marginally less lethal conditions, a narrow band where temperatures merely freeze conventional lubricants solid and ice tectonic cliffs mark the boundary where thermal stresses fracture the crust.

The thin atmosphere is laced with ice crystals that refract what little light reaches the planet into strange halos and phantom images, false horizons and duplicated stars that make navigation by visual reference unreliable. On the dark side, the only illumination comes from starlight and the occasional distant aurora, painting the nitrogen ice plains in shades of deepest indigo that the human eye can barely distinguish from true black. The silence and darkness combine to create an environment that induces psychological distress in even experienced deep-space personnel.

Subglacial cavern systems riddle the twilight zone, carved by ancient geological processes when the planet may have been warmer. These caves maintain temperatures slightly above the surface average and are shielded from the ice crystal wind, making them the most viable locations for any human installation. Exploration of the cave networks has revealed extraordinary ice formations: crystalline structures that have grown undisturbed for millions of years into shapes of alien beauty, speleothems of frozen ammonia and methane in colors that have never been seen by any eye before human lights illuminated them.

Nox-Aeterna's value lies primarily in its volatiles: vast reserves of nitrogen, ammonia, and methane ice that could supply industrial operations across the system for centuries. The challenge is the cold, which exceeds the operational limits of most standard equipment and demands specialized engineering for every component. The subglacial caverns have been proposed as sites for pressurized habitation modules, sealed environments where the cave walls provide insulation and radiation shielding. But the darkness weighs on the soul, and personnel rotation schedules on Nox-Aeterna are the shortest of any active installation.
